Question
========
For which of the following purposes is XML typically used?

Answerlist
----------
* Exchanging data between different systems, for example through an API.
* Making remote procedure calls, such as with SOAP web services.
* Storing configuration and settings for an application.
* Saving a complex object, like an R list, as a text file (object serialization).
* Defining how a webpage should visually look, similar to CSS.


Solution
========
XML shows up in all sorts of places where data needs to move between systems or be saved in a structured, text-based way: APIs often exchange XML, SOAP web services use it to make remote procedure calls, many applications store their configuration and settings in XML files, and it is also a common way to serialize complex objects such as an R list into plain text. What XML is not typically used for is defining the visual appearance of a webpage - that is the role of a stylesheet language like CSS, not of XML itself.

Answerlist
----------
* True
* True
* True
* True
* False
